entries.exactSourceEnglish: Succession planting is a calendar habit, not a special crop.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Ku byala swibyariwa hi ku landzelelana i ntolovelo wa khalendara, a hi xibyariwa xo hlawuleka.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Ku byala swibyariwa hi ku landzelelana i ntolovelo wa khalendara, a hi xibyariwa xo hlawuleka.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Succession planting is a calendar habit, not a special crop.
entries.conditions: Copied byte-for-byte from the current Xitsonga registry.
entries.uncertainty: Existing machine draft; no changes or fluent approval implied.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Choose something your household actually eats often. Then sow a small amount of it, again and again.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Choose something your household actually eats often. Then sow a small amount of it, again and again.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Hlawula swakudya leswi ndyangu wa wena wu talaka ku swi dya. Kutani byala xitsongo xa swona, u tlhela u endla tano hi ku phindha-phindha.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Choose something your household often eats. Then sow a small amount of it repeatedly.
entries.conditions: Ordinary household choice and repeated small sowing translated; no crop, quantity, or interval added.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: ‘again and again’ rendered as repeated action.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Plant a short row every two to three weeks.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Plant a short row every two to three weeks.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Byala short row every two to three weeks.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Plant a short row every two to three weeks.
entries.conditions: Preserves exact numeric interval and short-row instruction; technical phrase and timing retained English.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: short row kept English pending local term confirmation.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Less waste during a glut. Fresh food for longer. And the labour spreads out across the season instead of landing on you all at once.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Ku lahleka ka swakudya ka hunguteka loko ku ri na ntshovelo wo tala. Ku va na swakudya swo tenga nkarhi wo leha. Ntirho wu hangalaka hi nkarhi wa nguva, ematshan'weni yo ku wu humelela hinkwawo hi nkarhi wun'we.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Ku lahleka ka swakudya ka hunguteka loko ku ri na ntshovelo wo tala. Ku va na swakudya swo tenga nkarhi wo leha. Ntirho wu hangalaka hi nkarhi wa nguva, ematshan'weni yo ku wu humelela hinkwawo hi nkarhi wun'we.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Less waste during a glut. Fresh food for longer. And the labour spreads out across the season instead of landing on you all at once.
entries.conditions: Copied byte-for-byte from the current Xitsonga registry.
entries.uncertainty: Existing machine draft; no changes or fluent approval implied.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Separate sowings may reduce the risk of losing everything at once. They do not guarantee a harvest if difficult conditions continue.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Separate sowings may reduce the risk of losing everything at once. They do not guarantee a harvest if difficult conditions continue.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Separate sowings swi nga hunguta risk ya ku lahlekeriwa hi swilo hinkwaswo hi nkarhi wun'we. They do not guarantee a harvest if difficult conditions continue.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Separate sowings may reduce the risk of losing everything at once. They do not guarantee a harvest if difficult conditions continue.
entries.conditions: Preserves ‘may reduce’, risk, losing all at once, and the full no-guarantee/difficult-conditions clause verbatim.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: technical terms and no-guarantee condition remain exact English.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Which fast crop could you sow in small batches? Decide on one, and start it this week.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Which fast crop could you sow in small batches? Decide on one, and start it this week.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Hi xihi fast crop lexi u nga xi byalaka hi small batches? Hlawula xin'we, u sungula hi vhege leyi.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Which fast crop could you sow in small batches? Choose one and start it this week.
entries.conditions: Keeps ‘fast crop’ and ‘small batches’ exact; preserves the one-choice and this-week instructions.
entries.uncertainty: No interpretation of fast crop as fast-growing or short-season has been added.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Here's what it looks like in practice.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Here's what it looks like in practice.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Hi leswi swi langutekaka hakona hi ku tirhisa.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: This is what it looks like in practice.
entries.conditions: Ordinary framing translated; no new instruction.
entries.uncertainty: Low.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Sow one. Then two to three weeks later, sow two. Then sow three. Then sow four.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Sow one. Then two to three weeks later, sow two. Then sow three. Then sow four.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Byala xin'we. Then two to three weeks later, byala xa vumbirhi. Kutani byala xa vunharhu. Kutani byala xa vumune.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Sow one. Then two to three weeks later, sow the second. Then sow the third. Then sow the fourth.
entries.conditions: Preserves order of four sowings and keeps the exact two-to-three-week interval in English.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: numeric interval held exact; verify ordinal grammar in Xitsonga.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: With suitable crop timing, harvests can begin to overlap. The first batch will not always be ready by the fourth sowing.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: With suitable crop timing, harvests can begin to overlap. The first batch will not always be ready by the fourth sowing.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Loko crop timing yi lulamile, harvests can begin to overlap. The first batch will not always be ready by the fourth sowing.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: With suitable crop timing, harvests can begin to overlap. The first batch will not always be ready by the fourth sowing.
entries.conditions: Preserves suitable timing condition, ‘can begin’, and the explicit not-always-by-fourth-sowing qualification exactly.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: only opening condition translated; outcome qualifiers and harvest sequence stay exact English.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Two to three weeks is a starting rhythm, not a law. A cool-season leaf crop may hold longer. Heat may speed things up, or cause a failure.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Two to three weeks is a starting rhythm, not a law. A cool-season leaf crop may hold longer. Heat may speed things up, or cause a failure.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Two to three weeks i starting rhythm, a hi nawu. A cool-season leaf crop may hold longer. Heat may speed things up, or cause a failure.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Two to three weeks is a starting rhythm, not a law. A cool-season leaf crop may hold longer. Heat may speed things up or cause a failure.
entries.conditions: Preserves exact interval and both ‘may’ qualifiers; technical seasonal crop and heat clauses kept exact.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: first sentence partly translated; remaining conditional claims exact.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Watch what your own garden does, and adjust the interval. That observation is the skill.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Watch what your own garden does, and adjust the interval. That observation is the skill.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Intercropping is not just crowding different plants together. Each plant needs a job, and enough space to do it.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Intercropping is not just crowding different plants together. Each plant needs a job, and enough space to do it.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Intercropping is not just crowding different plants together. Xibyariwa xin'wana ni xin'wana xi lava role ya xona, ni space leyi eneleke ku yi endla.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Intercropping is not just crowding different plants together. Each plant needs its own role and enough space to do it.
entries.conditions: The first sentence remains exact English because the previous draft could lose physical crowding. The ordinary role/space sentence is translated while retaining the difficult terms.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: role and space terms remain English loans pending review.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Timing matters. Establish the maize first, so it's strong enough to carry the beans when they start to climb.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: The plants can still compete. Give them suitable space, water and light. Beans fix nitrogen with root bacteria, but do not assume they immediately feed the maize; nutrients in residues are released during decomposition.

entries.drafterBacktranslation: The plants can still compete. Give them suitable space, water and light. Beans fix nitrogen with root bacteria, but do not assume they immediately feed the maize; nutrients in residues are released during decomposition.
entries.conditions: Preserves possible competition and keeps all suitability, nitrogen fixation, root-bacteria, non-immediate-feeding, residue, and decomposition claims exact in English.
entries.uncertainty: Moderate: ‘can still compete’ translated with nga ha; all detailed technical claims remain exact.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: A household may have a hungry gap: weeks when stored food runs low before the next harvest is ready.
